items.title: Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Safety in AI Systems

source_refs.note: Unnumbered topic Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Safety in AI Systems under 8.2 as printed (PDF 114, printed 110).

blocks.text: Ethical AI development requires fairness to prevent discrimination, accountability to assign responsibility, transparency to explain how systems make decisions, and safety to protect users from harm. For example, if an AI system is used for student admission, it should not unfairly favor or reject students based on gender, region, language, or background. The university must also be able to explain why a student was selected or rejected and who is responsible if the system makes an unfair decision. Similarly, in healthcare, an AI system used for disease diagnosis must be tested carefully so that it does not give harmful or misleading results. These principles ensure that AI remains a tool for human benefit and does not create unintended negative consequences.
